_comment: Everything the wall reader is allowed to differ on, in one file. Nothing here is a fact about buildings - those live in the code. These are the numbers an office may legitimately set differently, and every one of them is a measurement in millimetres or in PDF points, never a coordinate taken from any particular drawing. This file is merged over the 'walls' section of plan_reading.json, so a setting given here wins and anything left out keeps its existing value.
_thickness_note: A wall is two parallel faces this far apart. Below the minimum it is a lining, a hatch boundary or a piece of joinery; above the maximum it is two separate walls with a room between them, or a boundary line paired with an eave.
_length_note: Anything shorter than the floor is furniture, hatching, a door swing or a fragment - never a wall. Between the floor and the connected minimum, a candidate is only kept when it actually meets another wall at a junction: a short stretch joined to the building is a pier, a return or a partition stub, while a short stretch joined to nothing is a bench top.
_tolerance_note: Two drawn pieces are the same face when they sit within this many points of the same line. A point is 1/72 inch, so it is a tolerance on the paper and means the same at any drawing scale. It must stay well under the thinnest wall the office builds, because a wall IS two lines a thickness apart: at 1:100 a tolerance of 3 points is 106 mm, which is wider than a 90 mm wall, so a wall's own two faces merge into one line and the wall disappears. Measured on one floor plan, going from 0.6 to 3 points took the walls at a thickness the office builds from 38 of 40 down to 21 of 27. The junction tolerance below is a different quantity and is deliberately much larger - it allows for an unclosed corner, not for a wall.
_overlap_note: Two parallel faces are one wall only when they run together for this share of the shorter of them. A face that shares a tenth of its length with another is passing it, not facing it.
_dimension_line_note: A dimension line is drawn thinner than a wall face, and where the PDF states a stroke width that is the cheapest way to tell them apart. Measured on the plan sets in use, an absolute threshold in points is the wrong instrument and it was turned off because of what it cost: offices draw wall lines at 0.25 and 0.35 pt, and a wall face recovered from a page read as a picture is one pixel wide, which is 0.36 pt at the resolution used - so a threshold of 0.5 pt threw away real walls on every plan set tried (one floor plan lost 30 of its 90 walls and 133 m of wall). Zero switches it off. Set it only after checking the weights the office actually plots walls at, and check the wall count before and after.
_hatching_note: Hatching is many parallel strokes a short distance apart, repeated across an area. A band of faces packed closer together than this, and more of them in the band than the number below, is hatching and is dropped before pairing. The count has to be generous, and this is why: measured at building scale, the gap between hatch strokes and the gap between a wall's skin, cavity, frame and lining are the same size, so separation alone cannot tell them apart - only how many there are in one place can. A band limit of 4 read a brick-veneer external wall as hatching and cost 48 m of real wall on one floor plan and 28 m on another. At 12 the guard is armed and touches nothing on any plan set tried, which is what a guard should do.
_junction_note: Walls meet at corners (L), at partitions running into them (T) and at crossings (+). Two walls are joined when each one's thickness band reaches the other's run, within the tolerance above. The result is a graph - walls are the nodes, junctions the edges - which is what later stages use to close rooms and to tell the outside of the building from the inside.
_outer_inner_note: An outer wall is one with nothing but open paper on one side of it: a ray cast out from it crosses no other wall before it leaves the building. That test is geometry, so it holds on an L-shaped or a U-shaped plan, where a rectangle around the building would not. A wall the ray test cannot decide is reported as unknown rather than guessed.
